info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package pubsub is your message bus: publish, subscribe, and durable streams your apps read at their own pace.

get.summary: Returns the org's streams, sorted by name.
get.description:
Returns the org's streams, sorted by name.

A stream is the durable log: it captures every message published to its
subjects and retains them by its own limits, independent of any consumer.
The listing is org-scoped server-side — one org can never see another's
streams, and the platform's own planes never appear.

post.summary: Creates a durable stream capturing the given subjects and returns it.
post.description:
Creates a durable stream capturing the given subjects and
returns it. 409 when the org already has a stream of that name; the subjects
are the org's own and cannot collide with another org's.

delete.summary: Removes one stream of the caller's org — its retained messages and its consumers with it — and answers 204 with no body.
delete.description:
Removes one stream of the caller's org — its retained messages
and its consumers with it — and answers 204 with no body. 404 when the org
has no stream of that name.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: Stream is the stream's name, from the path.

get.summary: Returns one stream of the caller's org — its configuration and its live state (messages, bytes, sequence range, consumer count).
get.description:
Returns one stream of the caller's org — its configuration and its
live state (messages, bytes, sequence range, consumer count). 404 when the
org has no stream of that name.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: Stream is the stream's name, from the path.

put.summary: Rewrites a stream's configuration — subjects, limits, discard — and returns the updated stream.
put.description:
Rewrites a stream's configuration — subjects, limits, discard —
and returns the updated stream. It is a PUT: the spec sent replaces the spec
held, with one reading for the enums a caller omits — an empty storage,
retention or discard keeps the stream's current one, because JetStream holds
storage and retention immutable and refuses a change with a 400 rather than
this door pretending it took.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: Stream is the stream to update, from the path.

get.summary: Returns one stream's consumers, sorted by name.
get.description:
Returns one stream's consumers, sorted by name. 404 when the
org has no stream of that name.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: Stream is the stream's name, from the path.

post.summary: Creates a durable consumer on one stream and returns it.
post.description:
Creates a durable consumer on one stream and returns it. A
consumer is a named cursor: it tracks what has been delivered and what is
acknowledged, so many workers can share it and none sees a message twice
outside redelivery. 409 when the stream already has a consumer of that name
with a different configuration.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: Stream is the stream to consume, from the path.

delete.summary: Removes one consumer — its cursor, not the stream's messages — and answers 204 with no body.
delete.description:
Removes one consumer — its cursor, not the stream's messages —
and answers 204 with no body. 404 when the stream or the consumer does not
exist.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: Stream is the stream, from the path.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the consumer, from the path.

get.summary: Returns one consumer of one org stream — its configuration and its cursor: delivered and acknowledged sequences, pending and redelivered counts.
get.description:
Returns one consumer of one org stream — its configuration and
its cursor: delivered and acknowledged sequences, pending and redelivered
counts. 404 when the stream or the consumer does not exist.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: Stream is the stream, from the path.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the consumer, from the path.

post.summary: Fetch pulls the next batch from a consumer and acknowledges it — the request/response way to consume a stream.
post.description:
Fetch pulls the next batch from a consumer and acknowledges it — the
request/response way to consume a stream. The hand-off is at-most-once: a
message returned here is acked here, so a caller that loses the response does
not see it again. Workers needing at-least-once delivery consume the same
consumer over the NATS port, where acks are theirs to send. An empty batch
after the wait is an empty page, not an error.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: Stream is the stream, from the path.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the consumer, from the path.

delete.summary: Removes one bucket of the caller's org — every key and every revision with it — and answers 204 with no body.
delete.description:
Removes one bucket of the caller's org — every key and every
revision with it — and answers 204 with no body. 404 when the org has no
bucket of that name.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Bucket is the bucket's name, from the path.

post.summary: Creates a KV bucket and returns it.
post.description:
Creates a KV bucket and returns it. A bucket is keyed state on
the same durable plane as the streams: each key holds up to History
revisions, entries can expire by TTL, and watchers on the NATS port see every
write. 409 when the org already has a bucket of that name.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description:
Bucket is the bucket's name within the org, from the path: 1–64 of
[A-Za-z0-9_], no dash.

delete.summary: Delete removes one key — a delete marker in the key's history, so watchers see it and Get answers 404 — and answers 204 with no body.
delete.description:
Delete removes one key — a delete marker in the key's history, so watchers
see it and Get answers 404 — and answers 204 with no body. 404 when the
bucket does not exist.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key is the key, from the path.

get.summary: Get returns one key's current value and revision.
get.description:
Get returns one key's current value and revision. 404 when the bucket does
not exist, the key was never written, or its latest revision is a delete.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key is the key, from the path.

put.summary: Put sets one key to one value and returns the revision the write created.
put.description:
Put sets one key to one value and returns the revision the write created.
Writes are versioned: each put is a new revision and the bucket retains up to
its History of them per key.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key is the key, from the path.

get.summary: History returns one key's retained revisions, oldest first — every put and every delete marker up to the bucket's History depth.
get.description:
History returns one key's retained revisions, oldest first — every put and
every delete marker up to the bucket's History depth. 404 when the bucket
does not exist or the key was never written.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key is the key, from the path.

post.summary: Publish puts one message on the org's bus.
post.description:
Publish puts one message on the org's bus. When a stream captures the subject
the write is DURABLE — the receipt names the stream and sequence only after
JetStream has it on storage, and a repeated Nats-Msg-Id header within the
dedup window answers duplicate instead of storing twice. When nothing
captures it, the message goes out core NATS: delivered to current
subscribers, receipt {ok}, nothing retained.

post.summary: Request sends one request on the org's bus and waits for one reply — the synchronous half of pub/sub, for callers speaking to a responder subscribed on the NATS port.
post.description:
Request sends one request on the org's bus and waits for one reply — the
synchronous half of pub/sub, for callers speaking to a responder subscribed
on the NATS port. 404 when nobody is listening on the subject; 408 when a
responder exists but no reply arrived within the timeout.

bucket.description: Bucket is the bucket's name within the org.

history.description: History is how many revisions each key keeps.

ttl.description: TTL is the entry expiry in seconds; 0 means none.

values.description: Values is how many values the bucket holds right now.

bucket.description:
Bucket is the bucket's name within the org, from the path: 1–64 of
[A-Za-z0-9_], no dash.

history.description: History is how many revisions each key keeps, 1–64. 0 means 1.

maxValue.description:
MaxValue caps one value's size in bytes. 0 or less means the server's
ceiling.

ttl.description: TTL expires entries after this many SECONDS. 0 means no expiry.

duplicate.description:
Duplicate is true when JetStream deduplicated the message by its
Nats-Msg-Id instead of storing it again.

ok.description: OK is true when the bus accepted the message.

seq.description: Seq is the message's sequence in that stream.

stream.description:
Stream is the stream that stored the message — absent when no stream
captures the subject and the message went out core (fire-and-forget).

data.description: Data is the payload as UTF-8 text.

headers.description: Headers are the message's headers, when it carries any.

seq.description: Seq is the message's stream sequence — fetched messages only.

subject.description: Subject is the message's subject in the org's own namespace.

time.description:
Time is when the stream stored the message, RFC3339 — fetched messages
only.

data.description:
Data is the payload, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text (typically JSON).
Binary payloads belong on the NATS port.

headers.description:
Headers are optional message headers, one value per name. A Nats-Msg-Id
header is JetStream's deduplication key: a repeat within the stream's
dedup window is acknowledged as duplicate rather than stored twice.

subject.description:
Subject is the subject to publish to, in the org's own namespace — e.g.
orders.created. No wildcards.

data.description: Data is the request payload, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text.

headers.description: Headers are optional request headers, one value per name.

subject.description: Subject is the subject a responder listens on, in the org's namespace.

timeoutMs.description:
TimeoutMs bounds the wait for a reply. 0 or less means the default of
5000; anything above 30000 is clamped to 30000.

ack.description: Ack is the acknowledgement discipline: explicit, none or all.

ackWait.description: AckWait is the redelivery timeout in seconds.

acked.description: Acked is the stream sequence acknowledged furthest.

deliver.description: Deliver is the starting point: all, last, new or lastPerSubject.

delivered.description: Delivered is the stream sequence delivered furthest.

filter.description: Filter is the subject filter, in the org's namespace; empty means all.

maxDeliver.description: MaxDeliver is the delivery-attempt cap; -1 means unlimited.

name.description: Name is the durable consumer name.

pending.description: Pending is how many messages await delivery.

redelivered.description: Redelivered is how many messages are being redelivered.

stream.description: Stream is the stream it consumes, in the org's view.

name.description: Name is the durable consumer name: 1–64 of [A-Za-z0-9_-].

stream.description: Stream is the stream to consume, from the path.

batch.description:
Batch is the most messages to return. 0 or less means 1; anything above
100 is clamped to 100.

name.description: Name is the consumer, from the path.

stream.description: Stream is the stream, from the path.

waitMs.description:
WaitMs is how long to wait for the batch to fill before answering with
what arrived. 0 or less means the default of 5000; clamped to 30000.

revision.description: Revision is the revision the write created.

created.description: Created is when this revision was written, RFC3339.

operation.description: Operation is what wrote the revision: put, del or purge.

revision.description: Revision is the entry's revision in the bucket.

value.description: Value is the value as UTF-8 text; empty for delete and purge markers.

data.description: Data are the key's retained revisions.

bucket.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

key.description: Key is the key, from the path.

value.description: Value is the value, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text (typically JSON).

data.description:
Data are the messages in this batch — empty when nothing was pending
within the wait.

bytes.description: Bytes is how many bytes the stream holds right now.

consumers.description: Consumers is how many consumers the stream carries.

created.description: Created is when the stream was created, RFC3339.

discard.description: Discard says which end gives way at the limits: old or new.

firstSeq.description: FirstSeq is the sequence of the oldest retained message.

lastSeq.description: LastSeq is the sequence of the newest message.

maxAge.description: MaxAge is the age cap in seconds; 0 means unlimited.

maxBytes.description: MaxBytes is the retained-byte cap; -1 means unlimited.

maxMsgs.description: MaxMsgs is the retained-message cap; -1 means unlimited.

messages.description: Messages is how many messages the stream holds right now.

name.description: Name is the stream's name within the org.

retention.description: Retention is the discipline: limits, interest or workqueue.

storage.description: Storage is the backend: file or memory.

subjects.description: Subjects are the subjects it captures, in the org's namespace.

stream.description: Stream is the stream to update, from the path.

name.description: Name is the stream's name within the org: 1–64 of [A-Za-z0-9_], no dash.
